text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired (PD#INC-9123) — node gpu-node-07 failed kubelet liveliness checks (kubelet NotReady). Auto-evacuation policy triggered. Autopager state: fired, suppressed=false

maya: acked oncall, jumping in. seeing NotReady across all pods scheduled on gpu-node-07. routing impact: small batch jobs failing quickstart tests.

sam: on it, paging serial console now. can someone grab recent kernel logs from node? might be kernel oops.

ashley: i'm pulling logs from stackdriver for gpu-node-07. quick grep shows repeated "kernel: [  123.456789] kernel panic - not syncing: fatal exception" entries around 2024-11-03T14:12:08Z.

ben: yikes. that matches the PagerDuty window. tagging hardware team in case it's bad nvme/gpu driver.

maya: cordon + drain plan:
```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-07
kubectl drain gpu-node-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --grace-period=30
```
we'll do a partial drain to let priority pods reschedule; i'm going to reduce replica count for a noisy job to speed up.

sam: serial console attached, i can see kernel oops stack trace and then reboot loop. no SSH. IPMI unresponsive for the last 30s but reconnecting now. grabbing dmesg dump via serial.

devops-bot: IPMI session initiated for host gpu-node-07 by sam. Power state: S5 -> transitioning.

ashley: copy of kernel trace snippet: 
"kernel: NMI: GPU watchdog timeout
kernel: Unable to handle kernel NULL pointer dereference at virtual address 0000000000000000
kernel: RIP: 0010:nv_driver_crash+0x1f4/0x260"
seems driver-related but could be hardware.

maya: customer-support, any live customer tickets referencing compute errors in last 10m?

customer-support: three new tickets flagged by monitoring: 'model inference errors' from tenant alpha-inc and 'runtime disconnect' from beta.app. I've reached out to them for severity.

ben: suggests we failover model-serving routes for critical customers to warm pool in us-west-2. Can we route alpha-inc to a dedicated fallthrough pool?

maya: initiating routing policy: promote model-variant stable-v3 in us-west-2, limit concurrency to protect pool. tagging oncall-runbooks: route-change should be quick.

sam: serial console confirms repeated XID 79 from GPU, followed by kernel OOPS. IPMI now shows SEL errors for PCIe PD. Filing for RMA if host doesn't recover after power cycle.

devops-bot: power cycle requested by sam. Expected downtime ~5m for host reboot.

maya: executing drain now. running: 
```
kubectl get pods -o wide --field-selector spec.nodeName=gpu-node-07
# scaling down non-critical replicaSets
kubectl -n batchscale scale rs noisy-worker --replicas=0
```

ashley: telemetry shows tail latency spike for a subset of inference requests during failover window ~14:12-14:16 UTC; overall P99 increased from 120ms -> 480ms for a few minutes. marking incident severity as SEV2 until full recovery.

customer-support: alpha-inc says they saw 5-10% error rate on inferences; offering status update and ETA. Beta.app reports intermittent disconnects but no downtime.

maya: update to Pd ops: PD#INC-9123 acknowledged. Oncall: maya, sam. Escalation: if not resolved in 15m escalate to infra-lead.

ben: added temporary routing rule: 
- shift 100% of alpha-inc calls to stable-v3-usw
- beta.app kept on best-effort retry policy

sam: host came back to life on reboot, but kubelet fails to fully start due to repeated kernel oops on module load. currently on reboot cycle 2. logs show nv_driver panic on init.

maya: marking node as quarantined. do NOT uncordon. creating incident ticket and runbook: link https://internal.redwood/infra/incidents/PD-9123 (placeholder).

ashley: start capturing crash dump with kdump if host survives long enough. if it reboots clean once, collect /proc/last_kmsg and send to hw team.

devops-bot: RMA ticket auto-created against vendor with ID RMA-56612 (pending confirmation).

maya: quick customer update: "We're aware of degraded inference success for a subset of requests in the US-West cluster due to a GPU host failure. We've routed impacted workloads to a healthy pool and expect remediation within ~1 hour. We'll update as we have more info." :thumbsup:

customer-support: alpha-inc accepted the temporary routing, asked for postmortem and whether model outputs were affected. logging that request.

sam: escalation check: 8m elapsed, still kernel oops on module init. recommending replacement hardware.

maya: escalating to infra-lead per policy. @ben please coordinate RMA and tenant communication follow-up.

ben: on it. I'll start inventory and schedule replacement. notifying sales for impacted customers.

maya: closing loop on immediate mitigation: traffic rerouted, node cordoned/drained, RMA initiated, customers notified. keeping PD open until postmortem. I'll hand over to night oncall at +45m for follow-up.

incident-bot: PD#INC-9123 status updated: acknowledged -> mitigated (services rerouted). Please update incident ticket with root cause hypothesis and timeline.

maya: thanks team. leaving handover notes: "kernel panic on GPU driver init causing kubelet NotReady and reboot-loop. probable faulty GPU/PCIe. RMA opened. customers routed to warm pool. SEV2->monitoring."

sam: leaving console session open in case node stabilizes; saving serial logs to /var/tmp/gpu-node-07-serial.log

ashley: grabbing crashdump and uploading to bug tracker.

customer-support: closing immediate tickets with status update; will reopen if customer sees further errors.

ben: will follow with procurement and hw team on next steps.

maya: handoff complete. ping me if anything flares. good job everyone. :heart:
